methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center cohort study (N=363 patients) from Serbia with systematic thyroid function testing every 6 weeks. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with log-rank tests; Cox proportional hazards regression with landmark analyses to address immortal-time bias. Appropriate statistical methods. However, single-center design, retrospective nature, limited molecular profiling (EGFR/ALK only), missing baseline variables (corticosteroids, autoimmune history, thyroid autoantibodies), and immature overall survival data limit rigor.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Addresses important clinical question about immune-related thyroid dysfunction as biomarker of immunotherapy efficacy in NSCLC. Directly relevant to treatment monitoring and patient counseling. Findings show strong association between irTD and improved PFS (HR 0.378, p<0.001). Suggests practical, readily detectable biomarker. LoE limited by single-center retrospective design and immature OS data.

reporting_quality.justification: Clear reporting of patient eligibility criteria, thyroid assessment methodology (TSH thresholds for hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, thyroiditis), and statistical methods including landmark analysis details. Results presented with confidence intervals and Kaplan-Meier curves. However, no explicit STROBE adherence statement. Data and code availability not mentioned.

novelty_literature.justification: Examines immune-related thyroid dysfunction as biomarker in NSCLC, building on existing literature showing irAEs associated with improved outcomes. Primary finding (irTD associated with longer PFS) consistent with prior studies by Chilelli, Cai, Cerić. Limited novelty; confirms known associations in single-center cohort. Adds to literature but does not represent paradigm shift.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear methods, results, and discussion. Comprehensive literature contextualization comparing findings to prior NSCLC cohorts. Good discussion of potential mechanisms (immune activation, treatment response). Transparent about limitations including single-center design, retrospective nature, immature OS, missing baseline variables, and generalizability concerns. Publication-ready quality.

key_strengths: Clinically homogeneous cohort of metastatic NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS ≥50% receiving uniform first-line pembrolizumab monotherapy
Systematic thyroid function testing every 6 weeks enhances detection of both symptomatic and subclinical events (30.3% incidence)
Robust analytical approach including landmark analyses at 3 and 6 months to mitigate immortal-time bias
Strong association between irTD and improved PFS confirmed across multiple analyses (crude: HR 0.378, p<0.001; 3-month landmark: HR 0.490; 6-month landmark: HR 0.587)
Clear clinical message: thyroid dysfunction is common, manageable, and may serve as practical biomarker of immune activation
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design from Serbia; limited generalizability to broader NSCLC populations and combination regimens
Incomplete molecular profiling (EGFR/ALK only); broader genomic testing (KRAS, STK11, KEAP1) not available during study period
Missing important baseline variables: corticosteroid exposure, autoimmune disease history, thyroid autoantibodies, detailed comorbidity burden
Thyroid testing interval (every 6 weeks) may have missed transient hyperthyroid phases, introducing imprecision in onset timing
Immature overall survival data; progression-free survival used as primary endpoint; long-term prognostic significance uncertain
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent retrospective cohort confirming known association between immune-related thyroid dysfunction and improved outcomes in PD-L1-high NSCLC. Suitable for Tier 3 journals (Cancer Immunology Research, Current Oncology) as real-world validation of biomarker with practical clinical applicability. Warrants larger prospective studies with mature OS data.
